subject: Egress origins, IP ownership & firewall entitlement for ACME private endpoint
messages:
From: Rohit Kumar <rohit.kumar@acmehealth.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: acme.security@acmehealth.com, ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private endpoint firewall/evidence ask — final IPs + audit evidence needed

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Security is finalizing the firewall and audit plan for our private deployment and we need a concise spec from Redwood we can hand to networking and audit. Specifically: 

- A canonical list of outbound IPs (control plane and runtime) that we can allow in our perimeter firewall, including any rotation/TTL guarantees.
- Whether Redwood will assert egress IP ownership (i.e., provide static tenant-assigned IPs) or whether we must NAT through our own customer-managed IPs.
- What evidence/log artifacts Redwood can provide for SOC2/third-party auditors showing which tenant/owner used which egress IP at a given timestamp.
- Port/protocol list (including any telemetry endpoints) and whether mutual TLS is supported for control-plane calls.

We have a draft internal firewall rulebook attached — it assumes static IPs. If Redwood requires ephemeral NAT we need to understand escrow options and a rotation SLA. Can you put together a short "entitlement + evidence" note for our auditors?

We'd like to get this onto the network change calendar by the end of the week.

Thanks,
Rohit
Rohit Kumar
Head of Platform Security, Acme Health
acme.security@acmehealth.com

Attachment: acme-fw-template.xlsx
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rohit Kumar <rohit.kumar@acmehealth.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, david.kim@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 13:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint firewall/evidence ask — final IPs + audit evidence needed

Rohit — thanks for the clear list. Summary below (high level) and attached a short spec pack and an IP-escrow template.

1) Two supported deployment egress models (choose one):
   - Customer-managed NAT (recommended for maximum control): your infra provides one or more static/elastic public IPs that outbound traffic from the private runtime/control-plane will NAT through. Redwood will operate entirely over that egress; customer is responsible for providing and updating the IP list.
   - Redwood-managed tenant IPs: Redwood assigns a dedicated (or ephemeral with escrow) public IP block per tenant. We operate the NAT and provide an "egress claim" CSV and audit evidence. This is easiest for customers who cannot manage NAT, but requires contractual IP custody (we can include SLA clauses).

2) Ports/protocols (minimal set):
   - 443 (HTTPS/TLS) to controlplane.redwood.com and model-hosts (required).
   - 8443 (TLS) for control-plane TCP backchannel (optional if you route telemetry separately).
   - 53 UDP/TCP (DNS) or 853 (DNS over TLS) if you perform DNS egress filtering — see notes on DNS below.

3) TLS and identity:
   - We support mTLS for control-plane connections (client certs) and strongly recommend TLS 1.3 for all channels.
   - For tenant egress where your NAT masks SNI, we provide a cert/hostname allowlist and support SNI-preserving proxies; however, some inspection appliances require SNI passthrough — if you have those please call that out.

4) Auditing & evidence (what we can provide):
   - Per-request metadata in our audit logs that maps request -> tenant_id -> egress_ip -> timestamp (retention per contract).
   - Weekly CSV reports for the period you request and a signed attestations package for SOC2 review if agreed in contract.
   - For Redwood-managed IPs we can provide an "IP escrow" CSV (see attached template) that lists assigned addresses and rotation windows.

5) Rotation & TTL expectations:
   - If Redwood-managed ephemeral IPs are used we guarantee a rotation window >= 72 hours for any given IP without notice unless under emergency (DDoS mitigation).
   - If you supply your own IPs you control rotation — we only require a maintenance notification for any planned change with 48 hours lead where possible.

Next steps I propose:
- David and I will produce the short port/IP matrix and fill the escrow template for both models (attached).
- Marissa will own contractual language for the IP custody / audit clause if you choose Redwood-managed IPs.
- Can we schedule a 30-minute signoff with your network and audit teams on Thu or Fri?

Attachments: controlplane-egress-specs.pdf, egress-ip-escrow-template.csv

Thanks — looping David and Marissa for technical/contract follow-up.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Rohit Kumar <rohit.kumar@acmehealth.com>, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private endpoint firewall/evidence ask — final IPs + audit evidence needed

Rohit/Team — adding the technical detail Lauren promised. Below are specifics we'd like your network team to implement or confirm.

A) Exact endpoints to allow (egress from your private runtime):
   - controlplane.redwood.com: TCP 443 (TLS 1.3, optional mTLS) — control plane API and webhook callbacks.
   - telemetry.redwood-internal.net: TCP 8443 (TLS) — aggregated telemetry and billing events.
   - model-host-[region].redwood-models.net: TCP 443 (TLS) — model weight fetch / health checks.

B) IP behavior and rotation (Redwood-managed model):
   - Typical assigned egress block: a /29 or /27 depending on scale — we will list exact addresses in the escrow CSV.
   - Rotation policy: planned rotation windows are >= 72 hours. In emergency (eg sustained abuse) we may rotate more frequently and will notify you; rotation events are recorded in the audit artifact.

C) NAT and source port behaviour:
   - Our runtime expects stable source ports for long-lived connections (agent <-> model) where possible; please avoid aggressive source port randomization on your egress NAT for persistent connections.

D) DNS considerations:
   - We recommend allowing outbound DNS (53 UDP/TCP) to your DNS resolver. If you intercept/terminate DNS over TLS/SNI at network perimeter, ensure TLS passthrough for our model-host hostnames or configure the resolver to return the correct origin addresses; split-horizon resolvers are supported.

E) Audit evidence format and retention: 
   - Per-request log entries (JSON lines) with fields: timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, egress_ip, src_internal_id, target_host. We can provide these logs for the audit period as either a signed bundle (for SOC2) or as CSV extracts. Default retention is 90 days; extended retention terms available under enterprise plan.

F) Operational notes:
   - Health-check IPs may be different from runtime egress IPs during autoscale events; allow the assigned block and the controlplane domain names rather than individual ephemeral addresses if possible.

Attachment: tenant-egress-mapping.xlsx (blank template attached for your network to fill with customer-managed IPs and their owners).

If you confirm you want Redwood-managed IPs we will fill the escrow template and hand to you for sign-off. Happy to hop on a screenshare with your network ops team.

— David
David Kim
Director, Runtime Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren/David/Kim — the details are helpful. Two quick clarifications before we book change window: 

1) Rotation frequency: the 72-hour minimum on Redwood-managed ephemeral IPs is acceptable, but can you confirm how rotation events are surfaced? We need an automated artifact we can ingest (timestamp + old_ip + new_ip + reason).

2) Audit linkage: for SOC2 we need proof that maps egress_ip -> tenant_id at the minute level for a 30-day window. You've noted per-request metadata — can that be exported as a signed CSV (signed by Redwood) we can hand to auditors? Please confirm the signing process (PGP or signed PDF ledger).

If those two items are available we'll proceed to place a network change on Friday.

Best,
ACME Ops
Ops Team, Acme Health
